problems.title: Unavailable physics is encoded as zero violations
claim: Physical feedback is intended to measure collision and boundary violations, but the missing-file branch fills those fields with numeric zeros.
analysis: When the expected per-iteration physics file is absent, eval_scene assigns zero to OOB Objects and BBL objects and Unknown only to object count. No geometry has been examined, so neither zero is a measured empty violation set. The native present-file schema contains lists, so the fallback also changes type. The valid present-file branch preserves actual measurements; the defect is restricted to missing data.
result: The current release can feed unmeasured zeros into agent feedback. Whether any published scene used this fallback is unknown.
repair: Fail explicitly on the missing record, or use null plus an unavailable status handled by every consumer. This establishes that successful measurements came from actual records, without proving recovery or retry behavior.
problems.impact_rationale: A bounded missing-data release defect is demonstrated; reported physical table values are not shown false.
problems.existing_correction_status: The described correction remains a proposal; author adoption or a corresponding erratum is not established.

problems.title: Historical exports reuse terminal physics for every iteration
claim: Each exported iteration combines its action and perceptual score with physics loaded using the terminal index.
analysis: For iterations \(0,1,2\), suppose native physics records have object counts \((3,5,7)\) and collision counts \((2,1,0)\). The loop reads the terminal file each time, exporting \((7,7,7)\) and \((0,0,0)\) under distinct iteration labels. This is not a terminal-only schema because action/perception remain iteration-specific. Crucially, the terminal-only final aggregator reads the correct final entry, and direct current feedback uses its own index.
result: The historical trajectory is misindexed; this alone does not change a final-only physical metric or prove different generated scenes.
repair: Use the loop index for both the existence check and physics read, retaining the terminal index only in the complete export filename.
problems.impact_rationale: The issue corrupts intermediate provenance, while the inspected terminal aggregation is unaffected.
problems.existing_correction_status: The described correction remains a proposal; author adoption or a corresponding erratum is not established.

problems.title: Zero counted collisions has a bounded geometric meaning
problems.source_location: Section 4.2 and Table 3; Pipeline/evaluation geometry predicates; author public issue replies
claim: The physical metric excludes selected objects and uses positive penetration/volume thresholds rather than testing every mesh component for any overlap.
analysis: A positive overlap depth \(0.0005\,\mathrm m\) fails a strict \(d>0.001\,\mathrm m\) predicate. A watertight intersection volume \(10^{-5}\,\mathrm m^3\) fails the \(10^{-4}\,\mathrm m^3\) threshold even if depth passes. Rugs and internal components of composite assets can be excluded; prior author replies explain that choice. The boundary predicate uses a buffered floor footprint rather than full three-dimensional enclosure.
result: These are legitimate metric conventions requiring a scoped interpretation, not a newly established benchmark error or a proof of dynamic stability.
problems.impact_rationale: The concern narrows the metric’s domain; tolerances and selected-object conventions are not intrinsically erroneous.
problems.existing_correction_status: No applicable author correction was established in this inspection.

impact_rationale: Minor: two local record/feedback defects are supported; actual published terminal metric damage is not established.
